title: TS-16 Message admission and listing
description:
## Slice 2 ticket 16 of 40, phase notes: paths use `conversation/` (the workspace as it is on develop). Design source: `git show origin/docs/typescript-control-plane:docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md` (section 8, row 16); read sections 0.3, 2, 3 and 6 as needed. Read AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING_AGENT.md first. Never read or write `project/`; use `kbs` only.

## Goal
Implement POST and GET of channel messages: atomic seq allocation, mailbox writes for every participating bot, idempotency, participant checks, and the steer-or-new-turn transaction keyed by (channel, bot), exactly as sections 2.5 and 2.6 of the design doc.

## Kind
design-then-build: the behaviour and interfaces are fully specified below and in docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md. Where this text is silent and a decision would be needed, stop and report instead of inventing.

## Branch and commit
```text
git fetch origin
git switch -c ts/16-message-admission-and-listing origin/develop
...work, then...
git add <only the files listed under Files>
git commit -m "feat(conversation): message admission and listing

Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"
git push -u origin ts/16-message-admission-and-listing
```
Do NOT open a pull request; the orchestrator opens it. Commit messages contain no emojis.

## Files to create or change
- `conversation/src/domain/messages.ts`
- `conversation/src/http/routes/messages.ts`
- `conversation/src/pi/message-cache.ts` (in-memory LRU of Pi entry bodies keyed by S3 object key, max 500)
- `conversation/features-support/steps/message.steps.ts`

## Exported interface and error behavior
`postMessage(deps, {tenantId, channelId, authorKind, authorId, body, addressedToBotId, idempotencyKey}): Promise<{message: Message; turnId: string | null}>` and `listMessages(deps, {tenantId, channelId, afterSeq?}): Promise<Message[]>`. `Message = {message_id, channel_id, tenant_id, seq: number, author_kind, author_id, body, addressed_to_bot_id: string | null, created_at}`. Algorithm for post: (1) check Idempotency-Key; (2) atomic `ADD next_seq 1` on the channel meta item; (3) put one mailbox item per participating bot; (4) if addressed and that bot has no active turn: create the turn control record and `active_turn#{bot}` pointer via one conditional put (ticket 17 supplies createTurn; until it lands, this ticket defines the interface `TurnAdmission` and uses a stub) and return the new turn id; (5) if that bot's turn is `active` and not `closing`: steer = write the mailbox item under a TransactWrite condition on that turn record, return the EXISTING turn_id, no new turn; (6) a condition failure on `closing` retries as step 4 after the pointer clears. Listing follows section 2.6 steps 1-5. Status codes and error bodies per the Python handlers (python/src/chatticus/control_plane.py post_message and list_messages).

General rules: TypeScript ESM, `.ts` import suffixes as in conversation/src/storage/; tabs for indentation as in existing files; long clear names; no line comments; TSDoc on exported symbols; no emojis. Each Python exception class used by a ported function becomes an exported `Error` subclass with the same name and the same message text. Failures are thrown, never returned as magic values, unless the Python returned them.

## Behavior spec (Gherkin, ported unchanged)
Existing features that must pass under cucumber-js when this ticket closes. Do NOT edit these `.feature` files except where this ticket says a behavior changed.

## Notes
Behavior change 1 of section 0.3 applies: a second addressed post during an active turn steers. Scenarios in messages.feature that assert the old 409 must be changed in the same commit with the change flagged in the commit message; stop and report if any scenario outside that is affected.

## Stop rules
If anything in this ticket is wrong, ambiguous, impossible, or contradicted by the code you find (a Python line range does not match, a step has no Python match, a library API differs from what is written, a scenario cannot pass without changing its text), STOP and report to the orchestrator with the exact file, line and observation. Never improvise, never weaken or delete a scenario to make it pass, never add a fallback or a compatibility branch.

## Python to delete
No production Python is deleted by this ticket (the one big deletion is ticket 40). The only deletions allowed: the per-feature step file of each feature newly added to the manifest, because the manifest vitest requires it: features/steps/messages_steps.py (if it exists). Shared step files (control_plane_steps.py, capability_policy_steps.py, messaging_steps.py, organization_steps.py and the like) are never edited here; the last ticket that uses them leaves them for ticket 40.
